dedupe_keys.name: multilayerparis multilayer multimodal transport network graph of ile de france

description: MultilayerParis is a graph of the multimodal transport network of Île-de-France, modelled as layers for different transport modes that are interconnected into one multilayer graph. It contains three layers: the road network, the regional commuter train network serving Paris and its suburbs, and the metro network inside the city of Paris. Each node is a road intersection, a rail station or a metro station, and cross-layer edges model the transitions between modes during a trip. It was built by Vincent Gauthier and Fereshteh Asgari at Telecom SudParis from the road network of the French National Geographic Institute (IGN) and rail and metro data from OpenStreetMap, and it supports a 2016 article in Computer Communications. Coverage is one city region. The graph is provided as GraphML, GML and edge and vertex files, released as version 1.0 on Zenodo in December 2016 and free as open access, with the code on GitHub. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10; reuse terms therefore remain unverified.1016/j.comcom.2016.04.014) is CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0. It supports network flow and multimodal connectivity analysis, cascading failure and robustness studies of interdependent layers. It is related to the OSMnx toolkit catalogued here.
